purpose: Sources used to frame the comprehensive astrology research layer and its limitations

sources.title: The sun's position at birth is unrelated to subjective well-being: Debunking astrological claims
sources.note: 2024 study using a nationally representative U.S. sample (N=12,791); analyses found no robust association between Western zodiac signs and eight measured well-being outcomes.

sources.title: Testing multiple statistical hypotheses resulted in spurious associations: a study of astrological signs and health
sources.note: Large Ontario population study illustrating how multiple-hypothesis testing can produce apparently significant astrological-health associations that require validation.

sources.title: Asset Allocation and Diversification
sources.note: Investor.gov explains asset allocation, time horizon, risk tolerance and diversification.

sources.title: Diversify Your Investments
sources.note: Investor.gov explains diversification as a way to reduce concentration risk; it does not guarantee against losses.

sources.title: Beginners' Guide to Asset Allocation, Diversification, and Rebalancing
sources.note: Investor education on risk/reward, time horizon, asset allocation, diversification and rebalancing.

method_note: Western, Vedic, Chinese, numerology, marriage timing, career, health and investment correspondences in this app are presented as traditional/cultural/symbolic research material. They are not medical diagnoses, financial recommendations, or scientifically validated predictions. Exact astronomical chart calculations also require validated ephemeris data; the current engine labels its planetary calculations as approximate.
